instruction.what: The evidence validation (B5) of one subgroup, after its sweep, the gate before 3.1: the code checks of its observations (shown in `code_checks`), and the reading of every evidence observation of the subgroup (its own of S1 to 2.1, and the older ones on its occurrences kept as evidence) for whether it is true, founded and coherent with the others. Inner being is not judged here; the two validations are never run together.
read: Read the code checks first: a failing check names observations to repair (unmarked, no node, a word node missing a column without its reason, a trace to a deleted observation, two of one text, a B1 observation no sense traces, a sense the 2.1 observations on its occurrences do not trace, an older observation left open).

Take one observation at a time (`observations`, in the order of the steps): its text, basis and grounds against its verses (`verses`) and the observations it traces. Is it true of those verses? Does it say more than they show? Does it contradict another observation of the subgroup?
write: Fill `answer.observations`, one entry for each observation of the package: verdict true, with `why` (what in the verses and the data bears it out); or verdict repair, with `why` (what is wrong) and `actions`: the actions of the validation that repair it (cfg_setting validate.reading actions, each with its parameters, for example {"action": "restate", "oid": id, "new_text": ..., "checked": ..., "reason": ...}, or delete_neither, complete_node, add_trace).
A repair is checked as it is written; an observation that cannot be made true is deleted with its reason.

Then: Collection-Build.ps1 -Action RecordEvidence -File <the answer file> (-Check to preview), and ReadEvidence again until every evidence observation is read; the gate passes when all are read and the code checks pass.

keep.text: A sheet of validation actions is checked whole (every action named, its parameters complete) and written in one transaction: any action the tables refuse refuses the whole sheet and nothing is kept. -Check runs every action and rolls back. Every change is kept in ib_observation_change with its reason (RW-01); nothing is physically deleted.

A finding of the validation is repaired first: a wording that is untrue or stronger than its verse is restated and the restatement checked against the base data; a node missing a column is completed, or the reason the data cannot give it is recorded; a duplicate is consolidated; a node is deleted only when another live node carries its occurrence or it supports no finding of its observation. A finding is left open only when a named collection's validation will touch the observation: the deferral to that collection and the finding are recorded, and the check accepts it as deferred. A finding with no named owner is closed in the validation.

An older observation is deleted as consumed only when live observations carry its meaning: every word occurrence of it is on a live node of a carrier or named as not carried with its reason, the mapping is stated in words (what the old says, which carrier states each part), the traces to it are re-pointed or replaced, and the consumption is kept as `consumed_by`. An observation that holds more than one finding is split first.

An observation that is neither evidence nor inner being contributes nothing to the purposes of the observations (researcher, 2026-11-22): it is commented with its reason and the word occurrences no other live observation holds, then deleted. An observation already marked, or one another observation traces, is not deleted this way.

Evidence states what the data are or show, tied to a verse. Inner being states how something works in the inner being, based on evidence, a building block of the stage 5 claims. The marker (ib_observation.nature) follows the content and purpose of the observation, never its stage (RS-04): an observation of any stage may be inner being when it traces to evidence. One that states both is split. The marker is set when the observation is created, by the item that is answered (cfg_setting layer.reading items.<item>.nature); a finding file never sets it; the validation changes it only where the content shows the item's nature does not hold.

The validation runs in two layers, never concurrently: evidence first, then inner being. The inner-being layer is judged only when the evidence layer passes (every in-scope observation marked, none without a live node, no word node missing a required column without its reason, no live trace to a deleted observation, no two of one meaning). A later evidence change reopens only the inner-being rows it touches. In the build this gate is: step 3.1 does not open before the evidence layer passes, and step 3.3 does not close before both layers pass (cfg_setting layer.reading open_gate and closing_gate).
No observation is changed except by a reading, and every change is recorded with its reason. An observation no longer supported by the verse is soft-deleted, with the reason.
One observation per finding: the same description is never written twice. Applied to another verse, word or scope it gains a node on the existing observation.
Observation text is concise and tied to this verse's content, never a restatement of the word's dictionary sense. A transliteration is never given without its gloss.
Verse references are resolved fresh at write time, never taken from the text written. Relations are recorded only on evidence.
Missing data in the base extract is named as a gap, never substituted from memory or outside knowledge.

observations.text: In Act 8:20 Simon supposed God's gift could be bought, and Peter curses his silver: the thought tries to take what is given. In Luk 8:18 what one thinks he has will be taken away. In 2Ki 7:12 the king thinks the Syrians will take the people alive, in Mat 17:25 Jesus asks Simon what he thinks about from whom kings take tribute, and in 2Cor 10:5 every thought is taken captive to Christ.
observations.grounds: you thought you could obtain the gift of God with money

observations.text: In Neh 6:9 the enemies think the workers' hands will drop from the work, and Nehemiah asks God to strengthen his hands: the prayer answers the enemies' thought.
observations.grounds: But now, O God, strengthen my hands

observations.text: In Mat 6:7 the Gentiles pray thinking many words will be heard: a false thought about prayer. In Mat 26:53 Jesus asks whether they think he cannot appeal to his Father: the thought misjudges his power to ask. In 2Sa 14:15 the woman thought the king might grant her request.
observations.grounds: Do you think that I cannot appeal to my Father

observations.text: In Pro 12:5 the thoughts of the righteous are set against the counsels of the wicked: thought and counsel stand as the two sides. In Mat 22:16 and Mar 12:14 the questioners say Jesus teaches the way of God truly and does not care about anyone's standing.
observations.grounds: the counsels of the wicked are deceitful

observations.text: In Rom 1:21 those who knew God did not give thanks, and they became futile in their thinking: withholding thanks goes with the thinking becoming futile.
observations.grounds: they did not honor him as God or give thanks to him

observations.text: In Psa 139:23 the psalmist asks God to try him and know his thoughts: the thoughts are what the trying lays open.
observations.grounds: Try me and know my thoughts

observations.text: In Lam 1:9 Jerusalem took no thought of her future and now cries out in affliction: the affliction follows the lack of thought. In Phili 1:17 some think to afflict Paul in prison: the thought aims at affliction. In 1Cor 7:26 Paul judges in view of the present distress, and in Job 15:35 trouble is conceived.
observations.grounds: thinking to afflict me in my imprisonment

observations.text: In 1Sa 27:12 Achish trusted David, thinking David had made himself hated by Israel: the trust rests on a mistaken thought. In 2Ki 18:20 and Isa 36:5 the Rabshakeh asks in whom they trust and whether they think words are strength for war. In Isa 59:4 they rely on empty pleas while they conceive mischief, and in Mic 2:8 the passers-by go trustingly.
In Psa 119:59 the psalmist thinks on his ways and turns his feet to the testimonies: the thinking leads the turning. In Jer 3:19 the Lord thought Israel would not turn from following him.
observations.grounds: When I think on my ways, I turn my feet

observations.text: In Rom 14:14 no food is defiling by itself, yet it defiles the one who reckons it so: the thought makes the thing unclean for him. In 1Sa 20:26 Saul thinks David is absent because he is not clean: a mistaken thought. In Lam 1:9 Jerusalem's uncleanness is in her skirts and she took no thought of her end. In Num 5:28 and Judg 13:7 clean and unclean go with conceive in its bodily sense.
observations.grounds: it is unclean for anyone who thinks it unclean

observations.text: In Pro 21:29 the upright gives thought to his ways, set against the wicked who puts on a bold face: the upright is marked by considering his way.
observations.grounds: the upright gives thought to his ways

observations.text: In Judg 15:2 the father thought Samson utterly hated her, and in 1Sa 27:12 Achish thought David an utter stench to Israel: utter marks how fully the mistaken thought judges.
observations.grounds: He has made himself an utter stench to his people

observations.text: Discerning and understanding stand with the thoughts in 1Ch 28:9, Psa 139:2, Heb 4:12 and Mic 4:12: the Lord understands every plan and discerns the thoughts from afar, the word discerns the thoughts of the heart, and the nations do not understand the Lord's plan. In Psa 73:16 the psalmist's thinking how to understand wearies him.
observations.grounds: you discern my thoughts from afar

observations.text: Wisdom and folly in thought: in Pro 14:15 the prudent gives thought to his steps, in Pro 18:2 the fool prefers airing his opinion to understanding, in 1Cor 3:18 the one who thinks himself wise must become a fool, and in 1Cor 3:20 the reasonings of the clever are futile before the Lord. In Ecc 9:10 there is no thought or wisdom in Sheol, in Dan 2:30 Daniel disclaims any wisdom of his own, in 2Sa 14:17 the king discerns good and evil, and in 1Cor 7:40 Paul gives his judgment.
observations.grounds: the prudent gives thought to his steps

observations.text: In Jos 22:28 the tribes thought the altar would be a witness between them and their descendants: the thought looks ahead to a later dispute. In Mat 15:19 false witness comes out of the heart with evil thoughts, and in Joh 5:39 the Scriptures that the hearers think hold life bear witness to Jesus.
observations.grounds: it is they that bear witness about me

The intention of the heart: "every intention of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually" (Gen 6:5); "the intention of man's heart is evil from his youth" (Gen 8:21) — said by the Lord "in his heart"; "keep forever such purposes and thoughts in the hearts of your people, and direct their hearts toward you" (1Ch 29:18); "the Lord searches all hearts and understands every plan and thought" (1Ch 28:9); "disclose the purposes of the heart" (1Co 4:5)
Face: The righteous' thoughts; Verses: Pro 12:5 ("the thoughts of the righteous are just")

4.2 What thoughts are: Inner speech. 21 of the rows (H0559, *ʾāmar*, "to say") are places where the Hebrew says "he *said*" and the ESV renders it "he thought," as in 1 Samuel 18:11: "Saul thought, 'I will pin David…'" The Greek *dialogismos* (G1261) and *logismos* (G3053) are also built on *logos*, "word" [lexical]. In these texts, to think is to speak inwardly. *Caveat:* how many rows show this depends on the ESV's choices.; Devising or planning. H4284 *maḥăšāvāh* (from H2803 *ḥāšav*, "to devise"). These thoughts are designs with a direction. They can be just (Proverbs 12:5), evil (Isaiah 59:7), or God's own plan (Micah 4:12). Because they point somewhere, they can be judged, and they can be abandoned (Isaiah 55:7).; Likening, or interpreting. H1819 *dāmāh* ("to resemble") is used in Psalm 50:21: "you thought that I was one like yourself." Many rows record thoughts that were wrong: Genesis 38:15, Mark 6:49, Luke 24:37, Matthew 20:10, Acts 12:9, Judges 3:24 and 2 Kings 5:11. So a thought is a reading of reality, not reality itself.; Something that grows and matures. 1 Corinthians 13:11: "I thought like a child … I gave up childish ways."; Transient, yet weighty. Human thoughts are "but a breath" (Psalm 94:11) and "futile" (1 Corinthians 3:20). Yet God weighs them (Proverbs 15:26), and before the flood they were the measure of human wickedness (Genesis 6:5). God's thoughts, by contrast, are "very deep" (Psalm 92:5), "vast" (Psalm 139:17) and "higher" (Isaiah 55:8–9).
The English word "thought" picks up rows that aren't about the inner life. 1 Timothy 3:7 ("well thought of"), Acts 15:38, 2 Corinthians 9:5 and Philippians 2:25.

One word covers both inner reasoning and outward dispute. *Dialogismos* is rendered "thoughts" (Mark 7:21), but also "quarreling" (1 Timothy 2:8), "disputing" (Philippians 2:14) and "opinions" (Romans 14:1). The same activity happens inside a person as an inner conversation and between people as argument.

Face: Thinking and considering; Verses: Psa 73:16; 77:5; 119:59; Job 6:26; 35:2; Jer 23:27; Isa 29:16; What differs: Alone it is "a wearisome task" (Psa 73:16) "until I went into the sanctuary of God; then I discerned their end" (73:17). Turned on oneself it turns the feet (119:59). Turned on others' forgetting: "think to make my people forget my name by their dreams" (Jer 23:27); Why (basis): Where the thinking is done changes what it can see (S)

*raʿyôn* (Aramaic) | Night thoughts that carry revelation · thoughts that alarm | Dan 2:29–30 · Dan 4:19; 5:6, 10; 7:28 | The same night thoughts become revelation when God makes them known and an interpreter speaks (2:29–30; 5:10–12 points to Daniel). Without that they alarm, and the body shows it. Daniel's own alarm is kept, not acted on: "but I kept the matter in my heart" (7:28) (S)
*rēaʿ* | My thoughts known by God · God's thoughts precious to me | Psa 139:2 · 139:17 | The same word runs both ways in one psalm (S)

*ʿaštût* | Thought shaped by ease | Job 12:5 | "In the thought of one who is at ease there is contempt for misfortune" (S). Comfort is a circumstance that changes thought's character. Compare Amo 6:1–5 and "the nations that are at ease" (Zec 1:15, anger strand)

*logizomai* | God reckons righteousness · God does not count sin · faith reckons God able · told to reckon oneself dead to sin · told to think on what is excellent · love does not reckon wrong · "may it not be charged" · others' estimate · suspicion · counting on boldness · claiming credit, denied · numbered with transgressors · counted as nothing · counted as offspring · wages counted as due, not gift · a calculation that became prophecy | Rom 4 (×11); Gal 3:6; Jam 2:23 · Rom 4:8; 2Co 5:19 · Heb 11:19 · Rom 6:11 · Phili 4:8 · 1Co 13:5 · 2Ti 4:16 · 1Co 4:1; 1Pe 5:12; 2Co 11:5; 12:6 · 2Co 10:2 · 2Co 10:2 · 2Co 3:5 · Luk 22:37 · Act 19:27 · Rom 9:8 · Rom 4:4 · Joh 11:50–51 | Who reckons (God, faith, love, the apostle, opponents); what is set to whose account (2Co 3:5: "Not that we are sufficient in ourselves to claim anything as coming from us"); whether it counts up wrong (2Co 10:2 suspect) or refuses to (1Co 13:5). Caiaphas reckons a death to be expedient (Joh 11:50), and "he did not say this of his own accord, but … prophesied" (11:51): a cold calculation is taken up into God's purpose, as in Gen 50:20 (S/R). Tagging notes: Mar 11:31 "discussed" and Joh 11:50 "understand" (OT-H3)

*dianoia* | The mind given wholly to love God · the mind hostile · the mind darkened because of hardness of heart · the mind's desires, "children of wrath" · proud in the thoughts of their hearts · laws written on minds · minds prepared · a sincere mind stirred · understanding given | Mat 22:37; Mar 12:30; Luk 10:27 · Col 1:21 · Eph 4:18 · Eph 2:3 · Luk 1:51 · Heb 8:10; 10:16 · 1Pe 1:13 · 2Pe 3:1 · 1Jo 5:20 | Eph 4:18 states the causal direction: "darkened in their understanding … due to their hardness of heart." The heart's state changes the mind's character (S). Eph 2:3 links the mind's desires to wrath (anger strand)

A plan or purpose: H2803I (1Sa 18:25, Psa 40:17), G2233 (2Cor 9:5, Phili 2:25). Thought as a noun: H4284 (1Ch 28:9), H6248 (Job 12:5), H2808 (Ecc 9:10), H7808 (Amo 4:13), G3540 (2Cor 10:5), H1697G with H1961 (Deu 15:9).
